title: Pauri 6, meaning: jewels within
hookLine: pilgrimage bathing is worth it only if it pleases Him; the mind holds jewels when it hears the Guru's teaching (Japji 6)

cards: A man spends his whole life traveling the world looking for treasure, comes home poor, and then finds it buried under his own kitchen floor. People tell that old story in many cultures.
So often the looking goes far away, for what's close. Guru Nanak's sixth pauri says something like it, standing on yesterday's riverbank. The jewels, it says, are closer than the river.

teach.h: A BATH IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE HEART.
teach.b: Here's the pauri in plain words, following Macauliffe. If I please Him, that is my pilgrimage bath; if I don't, what good is bathing? I look at the whole creation: without His grace, what does anyone receive?
Then: mat vich ratan javaahar maanik, je ik gur kee sikh sunee.
In the mind there are jewels, gems and rubies, if you listen to even one teaching of the Guru. Mat is the mind, the understanding.
Ratan, javaahar, maanik: three words for precious stones, piled up so you feel the weight.

teach.h: SIKH — ONE WHO HEARS THE TEACHING.
teach.b: The key is sikh, which here means a teaching, an instruction. The word Sikh itself is usually traced to the same root: a learner, one who receives the teaching.
On that reading, a Sikh is someone who listens for the jewels. Notice what the pauri doesn't say.
It doesn't mock anyone for bathing in a river; Guru Nanak stood at those rivers, the stories say, and people still come to them.
It says the bath is only as good as the heart that steps into it, and that what really washes and enriches a person is inside, waiting to be heard.
Then the refrain returns: O Guru, give me this one understanding, that there is one Giver of all beings; may I not forget Him. The jewels were never imported from somewhere else.
They're what's left when one teaching is actually heard. One, not a library.

how: Sikhs recite the sixth pauri each morning; its line about jewels in the mind is quoted in talks on why listening to Gurbani matters.

games.q: what's inside the pauri — tap the pairs.
p: a teaching; one who hears it

s: the pauri mocks people who bathe at holy rivers
it says the bath is only as good as the heart that steps into it.
hearing even one teaching of the Guru fills the mind with jewels
je ik gur kee sikh sunee: if you hear even one.
the word Sikh shares a root with the word for a teaching
a Sikh is a learner, one who receives the teaching.

games.q: where does the sixth pauri say the jewels, gems and rubies are?
o: at the bottom of the holy river.
in the mind, when one teaching of the Guru is heard.
games.why: mat vich ratan javaahar maanik: in the mind, if you hear even one teaching.

practice: Look inward, as if opening a small box you haven't opened in a while, and find one jewel in yourself: not something you've achieved but something you are, like patience that shows up when it matters, a way of making people laugh, or the attention you give a friend in trouble.
Hold it a moment and ask where it came from: who taught you, what line you once heard and kept. If you pray, you can thank the Giver with Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Mat. The mind, the understanding: what holds jewels, gems and rubies, when it hears even one teaching of the Guru.
